title: Day 23 — Dependency Resolver (Topological Sort)
prompt: The build runner needs to order tasks so each runs after its dependencies, pick a stable order, and fail cleanly on impossible (cyclic) dependencies. Given a graph of task -> its dependencies, how do you produce the order?

clarifications.answer: Every task must appear after all of its dependencies in the result.
When several tasks are ready at once, pick the alphabetically smallest first — so the output is stable.
If there's a cycle (including a self-dependency), raise CycleError. Don't hang or return a partial order.
A dependency that never appears as a key is a task with no dependencies of its own — a root.
A dependency listed twice should behave the same as once.
Kahn's algorithm (in-degree + a min-heap of ready nodes) gives both the deterministic order and the cycle check for free.

hints: Which nodes can go first? The ones nothing depends on being done yet — in-degree zero.
Use Kahn's algorithm: repeatedly take a ready (in-degree 0) node, append it, and decrement its dependents. A min-heap of ready nodes gives the alphabetical tie-break.
If you process fewer nodes than the graph contains, the remaining ones are in a cycle -> raise CycleError. Remember to include dep-only nodes in the node set.
